answers: The professor thought it was possible to reduce the effects of reverberation by removing the low-energy segments. He thought a VAD-like approach would work. This would make it so that the model was more likely to keep an echo than throw out speech.
turn_texts: The professor discussed the issue of echoes and reverberation, suggesting that they could be problematic for the system due to the low-energy parts of speech where reverberation is most audible. He proposed that using a VAD (Voice Activity Detection) approach to set very low or near-zero values for very low-energy sections could help in reducing these issues. Additionally, he mentioned that high-pass filtering, similar to what Hirsch did in the late 80s, could be considered to reduce reverberation effects. The professor also suggested that if echoes were part of the problem, they could be removed in a conservative way to keep speech intact.
